newsitem.title: USA: FCC chief voices concern over TV liquor ads.
newsitem.headline: FCC chief voices concern over TV liquor ads.

text.p: The chairman of the Federal Communications Commission expressed concern Monday about the impact of television ads for liquor on children after a recent spate of ads by Seagram Co. Ltd.

Reed Hundt's comments, in a speech to the American Academy of Pediatrics in Boston, suggested the FCC chief was weighing whether new rules were needed after Seagram ended the liquor industry's decades-old moratorium of not advertising on TV.

Hundt appealed for public help "to guarantee that every child has reasonable protection from the media's capacity to do harm," including "advertising hard liquor to an audience of children." He urged members of the public to let his agency know their thoughts on the issue.
"Halloween is supposed to be one of the best nights of the year for kids. But in some markets there's something to be real afraid of this year," Hundt said.
"Halloween is one of the biggest drinking nights of the year, and to boost sales even higher, some broadcasters have started carrying distilled spirits advertising for the first time in my lifetime."

Seagam's ads, which began appearing in June, spawned controversy in the liquor industry and elsewhere and prompted criticism from members of Congress and President Clinton. Other liquor advertisers have said they will follow Seagram's lead.
Earlier this month Hundt said he would consult with other top FCC officials "to discuss appropriate procedure for responding to this situation."
In Monday's speech, Hundt asked the public to respond to the FCC about the ad campaign, especially what it means to children.
"Is that what the public wants done with the public's property of the airwaves. Will you let us know at the FCC? Won't you help us figure out how to think about liquor ads?" he said.
Also on Monday, the FCC sent letters to four TV stations in New Hampshire and Texas, and to the Telemundo Group in New York, asking for information about the airing of liquor ads.
